- Overestimate prices after strong sentiment spikes (positive sentiment > 0.4) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct quickly.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is weak or negative (sentiment < 0.1) — model misses downward momentum or fails to adjust for bearish signals.
- Lag in price correction: model often delays reacting to sentiment shifts — especially when sentiment turns negative, forecast remains high for 2–3 days.
- Mean reversion bias: model overweights recent highs and fails to anticipate pullbacks — especially in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish.
- Overshoot after sharp upward moves: model forecasts peak too high after sentiment spikes, then undercorrects in subsequent days.
- Sentiment-driven bias: when sentiment is consistently positive, model overestimates; when sentiment is consistently negative, model underestimates — adjust forecast by 5–10% downward if sentiment < 0.1, upward if > 0.4.
- Horizon mismatch: 30-day forecasts often overreact to short-term sentiment — model should smooth out sentiment-driven volatility over longer horizons.
